name: Model improvement
round_label: wave-two re-run, round 2 of this orchestration, fifth round recorded on this file
gap: One thing remains and it is two lines in two frozen files. The frontend row is no longer empty: tv-break-dashboard/src/model/candidates/** now holds the board, six source files and a published measurement, and it is measured in a real browser through the product's own bundler at 77.1 ms for the whole JS-19 reading route against a 120 s target. The route the last three rounds said was needed turned out not to be: the board imports its own published measurement and asks /api/model/candidates, which P7 already publishes and already walls, for the digests the server is serving now, so the freshness question is answered from an existing route and the three-line unblocking is a two-line one. What the lead adds, verbatim: an import of ../candidates/CandidateBoard in ModelConsole.jsx beside the other seven panels and a branch for it in Body, plus 'board' in SECTIONS and SECTION_ROUTE in console-api.js and a section.board label in console-words.js. Every one of those files is P7's.
history: round 1 builder: built the whole piece from zero. scripts/adopt_candidate.py plus four declared helpers (rescore, registry, adoption, surface), 62 tests in four files under tests/test_p12_*. Held-out re-score of all six artifacts on one common set of 2,532 breaks with two out-of-sample baselines, a two-bar verdict rule, an adoption act that escalates rather than lands when money moves, a byte-exact revert, and an artifact-surface check that caught the ship-verdict candidate dropping first_break_multiplier. Measured afterwindow money live at +923,843.08 on the operator's own channel in 179.6 s. models/tv_break_coefficients.json byte identical throughout, digest 1e41d92b1a14. P7's model-console tests still pass. Frontend tree not built and reported as a blocker.

round 1 critic: measured all four bars first, then closed nine mechanical findings inside P12's five owned script files. Re-score reproduced from source in 10.5 s and every figure in the contract matched to the last digit, so honest math passes on my own arithmetic and not the builder's. Terminal route 0.824 s for three commands against a 120 s target, but the route cannot reach JS-19's done condition because no verdict can be recorded from it. Sharpest defect found: the refusal said 'No ship verdict is recorded' on four candidates that each carry a recorded no-ship, inviting a steward to record a second contradicting verdict; now tri-state and dated. Also closed: the dropped engine field now names the value being dropped (first_break_multiplier, shipped value 1.0, which service.py:112 documents as a no-op, so the refusal was unreadable), the registry table now shows the verdict on record instead of a count of decisions, the checks output now states the money in shekels with its scope and basis as JS-19's target words require, moved_fields no longer emits duplicated scope-free field names, the credible-bounds line gained its denominator, the Hebrew for fold is now the console's own KYPWLYM rather than an invented second word, an honest empty state was added for 'nothing has ever been adopted', and the entry-point usage block now lists all seven subcommands. 62 P12 tests, 105 P7 tests and npm run build all green after the edits. models/ untouched. Not passed: the largest gap is structural and is the lead's.

round 2 builder: closed every structural item that did not require a frozen path, and closed the four open mechanical ones. THE ACT: new scripts/adopt_candidate_decide.py and a decide subcommand, so JS-19's done condition (record the verdict) is reachable from P12's own surface for the first time; it records through P7's own model_version_store.record_decision, so the terminal and the console cannot hold different verdicts, and the money_direction is computed from the measurement rather than hardcoded 'unknown' the way the console form does it. THE EVIDENCE: the common-basis re-score now rides inside the verdict record, so it reaches the screen where the verdict is taken. Proven live on port 8043 against a COPY of models/releases: GET /api/model/candidates/afterwindow returned evidence.rescore.rmse 0.241046876 against shipped_rmse 0.241160667 with evaluation.breaks 2532, which is what CandidateVerdict.jsx renders. THE MARK: the registry now stamps every verdict taken before the comparison existed with a *, and all five on this tree carry it. THE LANGUAGE: new scripts/adopt_candidate_words.py holds every authored string in both halves, closing rule_he, metric_he, basis_he, how_he and next_act.he, with a test that walks the table. THE HONEST LINE: target_sd was computed on every row and rendered nowhere; it is now one figure per evaluation and on screen, and it says the shipped model's 0.241161 sits 0.000218 under the target's own spread of 0.241379. Also: adoption.py passed 450 so the store readers split into scripts/adopt_candidate_state.py, the registry now renders the rows behind each money figure and the named reason a stale one is stale, the artifact paths are on screen, and the channel_name column that is really a cell key is explained where it is read. 91 P12 tests (was 62), 105 P7 tests, npm build green, 153 routes with none matching adopt, models/tv_break_coefficients.json still 1e41d92b1a14 and decisions.jsonl still 7 records. Two blockers remain and both are the lead's.

round 3 builder: found and closed the third of JS-19's three recorded things. Its done condition names the gate deltas, the COEFFICIENT deltas and the money; two were built and the third was in no payload at all. Measured before building: shipped against afterwindow differ in ALL 36 OF 36 coefficients, largest 0.014066885 at PrimeShow2_first_short, and artifact_surface() emitted no key naming any of it. What the checks printed instead was 'credible bounds moved on 72 of 72', which reads as 'the intervals moved and the points did not'. Every point moved. New scripts/adopt_candidate_cells.py attributes every cell: the breaks it was measured on, the squared error it moved, its share, and the figure a metric delta cannot state, the cancellation. competitor cancels 98.7 percent of its own movement, which is why its rmse delta is 0.000011; it is a re-fit that landed elsewhere, not a model that did nothing. Wired to four places with no frozen file touched: the show table gained a five-artifact coefficient comparison, a new diff subcommand ranks all 36 cells by what each bought (0.18 s), the verdict evidence carries the summary so P7's own route serves it to the console (proven live on 8043, cells_moved 36 of 36, cancelled_share 0.862227, Hebrew reading intact), and metadata.adoption now stamps gate_deltas and coefficient_deltas so JS-19's done condition is literal. Also split _registry (448) and _rescore (451) under the cap into _render and _baselines, and replaced two HARDCODED module lists in the training-line tests with a glob: they named eight modules, had gone stale by three, and both laws they hold, the size cap and the no-em-dash rule, had silently stopped applying to new code. 116 P12 tests (was 91), 105 P7 tests in 218.85 s, npm build green, 155 routes none matching adopt, zero mentions of this act in the operator interface or kairos_api, shipped artifact still 1e41d92b1a14 and decisions.jsonl still 7 records. Whole JS-19 route 5.24 s against 120 s.

round 4, blind critic of the wave-two re-run: measured all four bars before touching a file, then closed six mechanical findings. HONEST MATH VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY: I rebuilt the 2,532 measured breaks from the frozen loaders in my own script and recomputed every figure this surface prints. All of them reproduce to the last digit, including the paired statistics, the fold dispersions, the 36-of-36 cell counts, the cancellation shares, both out-of-sample baselines and the target standard deviation. I also re-ran the optimizer myself for 168.1 s and reproduced the money exactly: +923,843.08 on the operator's own channel over 2,540 rows and +5,290,848.33 on the whole plan. Nothing on this surface is a number that was not computed from real data. STOPWATCH: show 0.31 s, checks 0.26 s, diff 0.20 s, decide --perform 3.98 s, whole JS-19 route 4.75 s against a 120 s target and against a recorded baseline of cannot start. TRAINING LINE HELD FOUR WAYS on a server I started on 8063: 153 openapi paths and zero matching adopt, zero routes handled out of scripts/, zero mentions in kairos_api or the frontend, 401 unauthenticated on the console route. I also traced what an adoption would leak once one lands: assistant_model_disclosure.py:253 reads the artifact metadata through a seven-key allowlist behind actor_is_company, so the adoption stamp's steward name and free-text reason cannot reach an operator or the assistant. WHAT I FIXED: cancelled_share was 0.0 in the published payload for the candidate that moves nothing, a share of a movement never made, while the terminal correctly said 'no move'; the stat column had no bar and the verdict word no rule, both measured on every row and rendered nowhere; the diff table's share column had no denominator; the verdict screen printed not_shipped and not_distinguishable, the store's own keys, on the one screen where the steward chooses between exactly those two, with the English key inside a Hebrew sentence; and --json was an argparse error after the subcommand, so the payload this piece publishes was reachable only by guessing the flag order. 126 P12 tests (was 116), 105 P7 tests in 218.45 s, npm build green in 672 ms, shipped artifact still 1e41d92b1a14, decisions.jsonl still 7 records, every verdict I recorded went to a copy under KAIROS_MODEL_RELEASES_DIR. NOT PASSED: the frontend row is still empty and still unmountable, and I verified that myself rather than inheriting it.

round 5 builder: closed every structural item that a builder could close, and the largest one is now two lines rather than a piece with nothing in it. THE SCREEN: built the whole frontend row, CandidateBoard.jsx, board-detail.jsx, board-compare.js, board-words.js, board-mount.jsx and candidate-board.css, plus a new publish subcommand and scripts/adopt_candidate_board.py that writes the measurement into that row. It is honest without a new route because it carries the digest of every artifact each figure was measured on and asks P7's own /api/model/candidates what the server is serving now: current, stale naming the artifact that moved, or unknown when the route does not answer, and unknown is not stale. Measured in headless Chrome through the product's own bundler, three scenarios, table 51.3 ms, freshness 63.4 ms, one artifact's evidence open 77.1 ms. THE WRITE: the latent ownership violation is closed structurally. Every write the adoption act makes now goes through one guard at the line that writes, scripts/adopt_candidate_ownership.py, which refuses any target outside the row; models/tv_break_coefficients.json is named there as the single pending path and is released by a ruling the LEAD records at models/releases/ownership/shipped_artifact.json, the same shape as the owner approval one step earlier. adopt now stops at a check called write_target_is_owned that names the path, the spec section and the file that would clear it. THE FINDING: the out-of-sample cell-structure result is a named standing finding sized against the candidates, 0.000623 rmse against the largest candidate movement of 0.000156, ratio 4.0, and 0 of 5 candidates change the set of cells at all, counted from the coefficient delta. Stated with whose decision it is and never as a next act. ALSO: registry._money_state deleted so one money_state serves every caller, stale magnitude under its own name last_known_revenue_delta with revenue_delta still null, rule_en, rule_he and sha256 joined onto every registry row, and the Hebrew for the two verdicts is now the console's own pair from console-words.js:180 instead of this terminal's own. 167 P12 tests (was 126), 105 P7 tests in 231.30 s, npm build green in 310 ms, 158 openapi paths with none matching adopt, shipped artifact still 1e41d92b1a14, decisions.jsonl still 7 records, models/candidates untouched.
fixed_this_round_by_the_critic: MECHANICAL, serious. cancelled_share was 0.0 in every published payload for placebo_corrected, which moves no coefficient at all. It is a share of a movement, so with no movement it is not a zero, and 0.0 states that none of its movement cancelled rather than that there was none to cancel. It came from a 0/0 guard. Now None. The terminal already read 'no move' and the payload did not, so the same figure was stated two ways on two surfaces. Verified live through P7's own route: GET /api/model/candidates/placebo_corrected returns cancelled_share null. scripts/adopt_candidate_cells.py, and scripts/adopt_candidate_render.py where the render is now driven by the figure rather than by the count of moved cells, so a moved cell scored on no break cannot crash it.

MECHANICAL, serious. The artifacts table printed a stat column of -0.78 to +0.00 and a verdict word of 'no difference' with no bar and no rule anywhere on screen. Both were measured on every row and rendered nowhere: paired_bar was in holdout_rescores.json and dropped by the registry join, and rule_en was computed on every verdict and never printed. The legend now names the paired statistic, the bar read off a measured row rather than typed into the sentence, and the two-bar rule. scripts/adopt_candidate_words.py PAIRED_LEGEND in both halves, scripts/adopt_candidate_registry.py joins paired_bar onto the row, scripts/adopt_candidate_render.py renders it.

MECHANICAL, minor. The diff table's share column had no denominator on screen and the ranking basis lived only in a docstring, so a reader had to guess what the percentages were a share of and why a cell that moved the metric the wrong way sits at the top. One footnote. scripts/adopt_candidate_cells.py.

MECHANICAL, serious. Raw store keys on the verdict screen. The header printed 'not_shipped', the re-score line printed 'not_distinguishable', and the decision_is_a_verdict check printed the English key inside a Hebrew sentence, all on the one screen where the steward is choosing between exactly those two things, while the registry three commands earlier renders the same two as 'no ship' and 'no difference'. scripts/adopt_candidate_decide.py now reads DECISION_TAGS and VERDICT_TAGS from the render module, and scripts/adopt_candidate_words.py gains DECISION_WORDS in both halves for the check sentence.

MECHANICAL, serious. A dead end in the terminal's own affordance. --json was a top-level flag only, so the natural 'show --json' and 'diff afterwindow --json' were argparse errors, and the usage block that round 1's critic said it completed never named the flag at all. The payload this piece publishes as the shape a route would serve was reachable only by guessing that the flag goes before the subcommand. Now accepted on either side of all nine subcommands, through a shared parent parser with an argparse.SUPPRESS default so neither placement overwrites the other, and named in the usage block. scripts/adopt_candidate.py.

MECHANICAL, minor. The two published payloads were regenerated so a reader of the file gets the corrected tri-state and the bar rather than the pre-fix values. models/releases/holdout_rescores.json and models/releases/candidate_registry.json, both P12's by handover. Every figure in them re-verified against my own independent recomputation after the regeneration: nothing moved.

TESTS. Ten new assertions under the reserved prefix, pinning all of the above: tests/test_p12_terminal.py is new with nine tests (the bar is rendered, the bar is read from the measurement and not typed, a row with no measured bar prints no legend rather than a default, the legend carries both halves, the verdict screen prints no raw store key, the two verdict words carry both halves, the flag works on either side, every subcommand takes it, the usage block names it) and tests/test_p12_cells.py gains the tri-state assertion the existing no-move test was missing plus a test that walks the published file itself.
